title: One normalized successor square for the strict finite reductions
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $A$ a commutative ring, $J\subset A$ an ideal, and $T$ the coefficient-sized pro-etale model site [lem-sfb-adic-finite-reduction-data]. Put $R=\underline A$, $q_n:R\to\underline{A/J^{n+1}}$, and $F_n=\operatorname{Res}_{q_n}\circ\operatorname{Change}_{q_n}$ on module sheaves. Use the strict ordinary reduction tower of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], whose successor is the actual quotient map on the scalar tensor factor. Let $P$ be a K-flat complex [def-pc-kflat-complex] of flat $R$-module sheaves [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], let $N\in D(R)$, and let $e:Q(P)\simeq N$. For each $n$, construct $c_n:U_n(N)\simeq Q(F_n(P))$ by derived scalar extension of $e^{-1}$, the universal scalar-extension computation on $P$, the inverse exact-restriction factorization resFactors, and the termwise evaluation identity. Here $U_n$ and $t_n:U_{n+1}\to U_n$ are precisely the normalized underlying reductions and adicFiniteTransition maps of [lem-sfb-adic-finite-reduction-data]. Then $Q(F_{n+1}(P)\to F_n(P))\,c_n^{-1}=c_{n+1}^{-1}t_n$ for every $n\geq0$. This is an equality of specified arrows, with no inverse-limit, completion, or existence-of-tower-isomorphism assertion.

proof.text: The uniqueness specification reductionStep_existsUnique identifies the chosen ordinary quotient successor with scalarTransition for the quotient, its quotient factor, and the smaller quotient. Apply this equality in each degree to identify the successor of reductionComplex with NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex of scalarTransition.

Reuse the proved scalar_transition_comparison calculation in the module of lem-sfb-adic-normalized-scalar-composition. For the literal composite ring map it compares the localized ordinary scalar transition, followed by resFactors and the inverse extension computation, with the normalized derived unit, exact restriction composition and balancing. Transport to the specified smaller quotient using adicFiniteConstantComp; equality elimination removes every transport in the verification.

Use the proved canonical_step_naturality calculation in the same scalar-composition module to move the levelwise images of e through the normalized derived step. Naturality of adicFiniteDresComp puts balancing inside the two restrictions, exactly as in adicFiniteTransition. Expand the specified level isomorphism inverses; the evaluation isomorphisms are reflexive transports and vanish. Substitute the degreewise successor identification and the transported scalar comparison.

lean.statement:
theorem adicFiniteStrictReduction_successor
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (A : Type (max v (u + 1))) [CommRing A] (J : Ideal A)
    (P : Cx (constant (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X) A))
    (hP : P.IsAcyclicTensorKFlat)
    (hflat : ∀ q : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlat (P.X q))
    (N : adicFiniteAmbient.{u, v} X A)
    (e : (Q (constant (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X) A)).obj P ≅ N)
    (n : ℕ) :
    ((reductionComplex (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X) A J false P).asFunctor ⋙
        Q (constant (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X) A)).map
          (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op ≫
        (adicFiniteStrictReductionLevel X A J P hP N e n).inv =
      (adicFiniteStrictReductionLevel X A J P hP N e (n + 1)).inv ≫
        adicFiniteTransition X J N n
